cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. As junior coordinator, you're responsible for the blocked sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran the whole event yesterday. You said I'd earned a promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. To senior coordinator. Still below me, but now you can supervise the plumber.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can only come after everyone leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll lock up too. I can't give building security to a junior.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns the sink by junior rank, A3 grants senior status still below A, and A5 uses that promotion to impose security duty.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 earned-promotion claim causes A3 nominal elevation; B4 late plumber causes A5 lockup responsibility justified by the elevated title.

relationship.evidence: B2 has done real event work and B4 reports a practical scheduling issue, giving A requests and facts to exploit.

heightening.evidence: B4 late attendance turns the supposed reward into an additional unwanted end-of-day duty.
